text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Today is the first anniversary of the signing of the Bosnia peace agreement in Dayton, Ohio.
- Croatian confectionary producer Kras says it is ready to return to Yugoslav markets, but first wants Yugoslav firms to repay a 3.5 million German mark debt.

- The gold jewlery maker Majdanpek says lowering of excise duties from 50 to 15 percent and sales tax from 20 to 24 percent helped its products be more competitive on domestic and foreign marktes. It plans to soon return to pre-sanctions export levels of one and a half tonnes of jewlery a year.
- A steady and concerning fall in turnover was registered at the Belgrade bourse in the January to October period.
- A two-day international conference on insurance opens in Belgrade.
- Average wage in October in Serbia was 797 dinars which is up 13.4 percent on the previous month according to the republic's statistics office.
- The federal constitutional court ruled that the exit tax introduced for all Yugoslav citizens is not unconstitutional.
- Spokesman of the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia Ivica Dacic urges the opposition to wait patiently for the electoral procedure to end, and for all objections to be examined as provided by law.
- Serbian lawyers continue their protest over high taxes by refusing to work in courts, saying taxes are not the only problem but also interpretation of existing laws.
- The Bosnian Serb assembly session will be held next week. International mediators said the Serb side agreed to exclude religious elements from the deputies' oath.
- Opposition leaders go on hunger strike over alleged theft of votes for the local elections, and call on authorities to "respect the legitimate will of the Serb people".
- Managers of public utilities expect to stay in their posts after the opposition takes over local councils, claiming they head professional and not political operations.

- First contract for import of 14,500 tonnes of wheat concluded even though the state claimed there was enough wheat in the country. Decision to be brought within a couple of days on an import contingent of 100,000 tonnes of wheat in 1997.
- Construction begins on a new road from Sjenica-Bare- Kumanica which will shorten the route from northern and central parts of Serbia to the Montenegrin coast.
